chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Bukayr and Jamil, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that the two (Ibn Bukayr and Jamil) said:

Regarding the Mutamatti' (one who performs Hajj al-Tamattu'), if he advances his Tawaf and Sa'y in Hajj, he was asked: 'Are they the same whether you advance or delay?' He said: 'They are the same, whether you advance or delay.'

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: Mutamatti', a pilgrim who performs Umrah and then Hajj in the same season
key_terms.سَعْيَهُ: His Sa'y (walking between Safa and Marwah)
key_terms.سِيَّانِ: They are the same / equal in ruling

ai.seo_question: Does the order of Tawaf and Sa'y matter for a Mutamatti' in Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that for the Mutamatti', the sequence of Tawaf al-Ifadah and Sa'y is flexible, establishing that either order renders the ritual valid. This ruling alleviates the burden on pilgrims, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of ease (*taysir*) in acts of worship, provided the essential components are completed within the Hajj season. The hadith underscores the permissibility of variation in ritual order without invalidating the Hajj, a key point in distinguishing between obligatory conditions and recommended sequences.
